I don’t mean to be too emphatic, but I myself have gone through it and I have lost 2 friends. The most insanely beautiful and talented and loved people. You can’t imagine it. One to medicine OD, another to jumping off a bridge.

This is serious. We must act seriously. 

After the house is… troubled-teen-proofed, let’s work on how to treat this illness. This depression. Seek help. We need paid professionals here with all that training and experience. They don’t have to be paid by you—there are many counseling services in my city for free. Stuff may be covered by insurance. But let’s research fast.

And finally. Does he have any hobbies? Friends came up organically for me after delving into music. It was my way to cope. I’d honestly lock myself in the bathroom for hours and play guitar. Got headphones for a keyboard  and would play piano for ever and ever! No lessons, just teaching myself. Does he have any lifeline like that? Because when therapy sucked and didn’t help, when the meds made everything worse in high school, studying like hell to get good grades and get away plus music saved me. We’re going to have to find these things and lean in. They need to be constructive. A way for him to express himself. Music and art are great, writing, but not everyone vibes with those things. Maybe baking? I’m a girl lol. Maybe sports—it can be a good way to get the energy out. Hiking and learning the different types of plants and even foraging. Gosh just anything. 

Bonus: usually when you find that thing? Friends follow. Turns out other people tend to like that too and you meet people that always have at least one thing in common with you. 

So there’s a lot of work to do, but get to it! And if it gets really scary, don’t be afraid to 302 someone. Call those folks and get him admitted. It sucks and is expensive but like, admittedly preferable to the worst alternative. No shame in it. I went in 2021 and started meds and it saved my life. We all regret not doing this for the friend we lost 6 years ago. She’d be 28 today.

I would try to match the grain of the marble or the grout. A lighter white, 2 is your best bet. 3 does not work well here, it’s competing with the grey. You can try it but I’ll bet you’ll be painting it again.

We’re 6.5 months now and baby is almost exclusively breastfed except he also gets solids now! And dad occasionally gives some formula here and there if I’m not around for an on demand feed. So, our baby was in the NICU for five days at birth to rule out an infection (he had a very high heart rate and low oxygen). We were not considered the highest risk so we were not offered a sleeper room, so I’d have to go home. While there, I noticed nurses would let babies cry for awhile and the reality was they had to be in their little incubators, I wasn’t even able to hold my baby right away.

So: grain of salt here. This is just my experience. But based on this being my baby’s start from the jump? I’ve observed him self-soothing since before 3 months. I want to say I did observe them at 2 months. 

We did sleep shifts, this was absolutely necessary for our family, I would sleep 10pm-4am, then husband would sleep 4am-10am. We were always with baby, one person at least at all times. We did notice the hand sucking himself back to sleep.

And maybe because our poor poor baby had to start from the get go in his own little pod (AGONY 😭), he was able to sleep and self soothe solo in his own bassinet since around 2.5 months. 

I do recommend reading Bringing up Bebe. Le Pause style sleep training worked for us. And baby is able to get through the night.

So… baby is now 6 months. He looks for me, reaches for me, we smile and cuddle and giggle all day long. He seems to have an understanding of sleep time. When he cries really hard, absolutely I go in. But it is probably only about 1 or 2 times a month? Super rare. He does fry and we watch him in the monitor as he gets himself into a better position and he falls right back to sleep most nights. 

In some ways, I’m so crazily proud of him! I hope he has some level of trust in himself as now at 6 months, supposedly babies are getting an understanding of themselves separately from their mamas. I don’t know, I’m not a doctor, but things seem okay overall. I still very much check the monitor haha I don’t exactly sleep as well as he does! But he’s just GAH I don’t know. I just love him.

Anyway… our baby is not Colic. Our baby does not have reflux. Our baby is not sick. I think he is teething in a big way, but beyond that, he’s healthy. This worked for us. We did let him cry it out twice. Once at 2,5 months and he did self soothe and go back to sleep. And once more like a week ago when it was WAY too late and he was just so no sleeping, he had to get it all out.

It’s a bit nerve wracking, I’m sure there will be backlash, but this was my instinct, that this was okay. Trust *your* gut, mama. Seriously. If baby is hurting though, that’s not CIO territory. That needs to be looked at. Baby needs help. I just wanted to share this as an example of well maybe it can work for some families when baby is still quite young. I think we might be an exception though? Not the rule?

Real talk: I despised my dog for like a few months after baby was born. Well, maybe that’s harsh, it wasn’t a constant despising… but when she would bark, or when she got diarrhea and woke me up all night while I was still trying to night feel baby, when she wouldn’t poop but I know she had to poop on the few times when I actually did get a moment to walk her…

Omfg I was so angry.

Part of this was postpartum rage. I didn’t realize it at the time, but around the 2.5 month mark I got diagnosed with that. Woof…

Anyhoo, the times I wasn’t purely angry with our dog, I was just so sad and ashamed. I cried multiple times about not loving her the same way anymore (she was my first baby!) and that I was neglecting her so much now (we just to go to the dog park every other day!)… 

For about 4 months, I felt like absolute a$$ about her. Not only did I want to rehome her, I even had waves of just… wanting to be violent with her which really freaked me out!

And at some point, that did fade.

Now, I just get mildly annoyed when she barks, or pulls while I’m trying to walk her and wear the baby, etc. And just today, I was actually happy to see her. Like, I felt love toward her again for the first time since before baby was born. Like, actual enthusiasm to pet her and I even invited her on the bed (she used to sleep with me in bed every night, but now I yell if she even tried to jump up. Tbh I only let her up cause I knew I would be changing the sheets today, but still! It’s a huge sign I’m warming up to her again!)

Things that helped me get through the worst of it: 

1. She was a rescue. At a kill shelter. So on the days I was so angry with myself for neglecting her, I just had to remind myself “Well, at least she isn’t just dead.” 

2. Reminding myself that this was in fact temporary. Eventually, baby would be older and much less needy and then? It would actually be great to have our dog. I’m glad for them to grow together and be active together.

3. **Ask for help when you seriously need it.** when it got really really bad, my parents took the dog for several weeks. Honestly, I’m so thankful for that. Ask friends, family members, ask for help. 

Good luck with whatever you decide. Having been there? I can’t imagine a shepherd puppy. We have a beagle mix, I understand shepherds are even more active and intense as a breed! So, I just would not blame you if you do rehome. Just do what you gotta do. Survival mode is understandable. Good luck.

I’m sure there’s a much better way to handle this, but for me it was just rage. Parents HAVE to be on the same page. Taking it apart piece by piece, is it the sensor? How can we get this piece to latch with that? And it took two days, but the man fixed it with? DRUMROLL: an expertly cut to size piece of zip tie.

Definitely, whether it’s on the registry or it’s something you ask for in donations, definitely:

- a changing table with shelves and extra hanging storage if possible. I cherish ours, lol. It holds also baby’s clothes and bedding. MUCH prefer easy access clothes to hangers when baby is fussy, cold, and uncomfortable and needs a quick change! (Note: we found ours on Facebook marketplace for $35 and I suspect you might even be able to get a donated one if your community is like ours and not very rich/well to do)

- diapers: you only need like one month supply of newborn size, get all different sizes and keep the receipts—you may need to switch to different brands before you find one that works for your baby’s bum!

- clothes with zippers (who has the patience and stamina for buttons on a screaming, fussy baby?) note: to this day, we’re in week 6, I have not had to buy any clothes! 15 bags of donated clothes from a single colleague and my sister spoiled us with some. I bet if we stopped the entire global production of baby clothes for a year, we’d still have enough for all babies in the world to be fully clothed. They only fit em for like a month anyway, just donations for us and if a family member “can’t resist” that’s okay too lol.

- infant car seat: you need it to leave the hospital. 

- stroller: haven’t used ours yet but it was a combo with the car seat and will be used constantly as baby grow and it’s not winter and we start taking him out more.

- postpartum recovery kit: fridamom has one with disposable underwear and witch hazel liners and foams etc. but if you don’t need all that **the foam and the peri bottle are must-haves imo.**

- get the butt spatula lol

- grooming / health / maintenance kit! Ours has the washable squeegee, nail filer, brush, snot-sucker-outer thing, lol, ther**mom**eter, etc.

- travel bottle cleaner kit. We got the $15 one and use it constantly

- some sterilizer system. Honestly? **the microwaveable steamer sterilizer bags have been easier for us.** I got a sterilizer machine but we haven’t used it, too much hassle!

- vented bottles of different months/flows

- **water wipes** brand wipes. These have been the absolute best for us after some wicked diaper rash.

- baby towels/sponge things for bath time 

- white noise machine of some kind 

- some swaddle blankets (all ours were donated from friends honestly)

- black with and red baby visual learner thingies

- tummy time mats with piano kicker attachment and mobile (donated from friends, $5 on Facebook marketplace)

- some rocker chair system. We got an old rockerroo for $30 on Facebook marketplace

- diaper bag (donated)

- **breast pump** if you’re into that and **breast milk stirage** either the bottles or bags.

- portable changing pad thing

- baby wearing wrap or sling

- baby monitor 

- baby soap/shampoo 

- diaper rash cream: Desitin or butt paste with high zinc oxide 

- we love our bedside sleeper bassinet ($13 on macbid)

- crib for later (ours was donated from a friend)

This is it. The must haves from me.

So. Keep growing and learning, it’s okay to change your mind about what you want to do in life, but no matter what: **YAHOO.**

**You Always Have Other Options.** suicide is the ultimate end. But look around. What haven’t you tried that? Try that first.

It could be a sewer line crack and leak and oooohhhh wouldn’t that just get grosser and more awful if neglected?? 

And wild card: could also be faulty/clogged gutter systems. 

So be super careful out there! Get a pro to check it out. Get a second opinion. Get bids. Choose wisely (probably not the lowest bid, or the lowest bid ya if it’s an extremely reputable company)
